ios.desc:
The coding curriculum used in over 50% of U.S. elementary schools, now at home! Kids go from solving their first maze at age 4 to writing real JavaScript by 5th grade, through games they actually ask to play.

LOVED BY KIDS, TRUSTED BY SCHOOLS
Rated 4.7 stars by 21,000+ families. Over 25 million downloads. Built with elementary teachers for more than a decade, and aligned to Common Core and CSTA standards, the same curriculum kids use in class.

WHAT KIDS LEARN
Ages 4-6 (no reading required): sequencing, patterns, and problem-solving through maze puzzles. This is the logic underneath all programming.
Ages 7-10: conditions, loops, functions, and variables, leading to real typed JavaScript
Every level builds critical thinking they'll use far beyond the screen

MORE THAN LESSONS
Kids design their own characters, build and share their own games, and jump into seasonal events. Creativity keeps them coming back long after the lesson ends.

USING KODABLE AT SCHOOL?
Sign in with your school account and your child's progress comes home with them. Some class content carries over free; Kodable Pro unlocks the full library at home.

BUILT FOR FAMILIES
No ads. Ever.
Works offline for road trips, flights, and waiting rooms
Designed to meet the strict privacy standards schools require

TEACHERS: A complete K-5 STEM curriculum with 80+ scripted lesson plans and Google Classroom, Clever, and roster integrations is available at kodable.com.

quotes.text:
None of the apps suggested actually help learn to think logically like you do when programming. There is ONE app I found that does just that and nothing more.

https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/kodable/id577673067?mt=8

Kodable. It's free but more importantly, it teaches kids about loops and sequencing commands - things you do on a day to day basis while programming (unless you're a functional programmer haha).
quotes.story_title: DragonBox: Secretly teach algebra to your children
